Nothing in the original file is changed or reinterpreted; this adds a reading the original's S1 cannot give. WHY IT IS NEEDED: `stale_px` is a SUM over swatches that fail for structurally different reasons, and #44 is now worked by two lanes with two mechanisms -- this lane's pushbuffer skew, and the texture lane's decoded-length hash gate that declines to re-upload at all (`blind=2` measured directly, on pass-2 4x4 and pass-2 8x8). AGENTS.md's rule applies exactly: a class count is a count of pixels a mechanism TOUCHES, not of pixels it is solely responsible for, and subtracting one from a differing total assumes an additivity these classes do not have. Judging a two-cause capture on one total is how a correct fix gets reverted. THE SPLIT, computed on the published ten-run noise floor (dispatch 1789255594-exp54-stst-correct-3660183, reproduced on this tree to the pixel: stale_px 146/0/2352/0/0/2430/0/1847/5640/181, races_lost 1/0/2/0/0/3/0/2/3/1, unexplained_px 0 on every run): of 12,596 wrong pixels in 12 failing swatches, TORN is 8 swatches and 3,852 px (30.6%), COMPLETE is 3 swatches and 8,064 px (64.0%), NO-SUCCESSOR is 1 swatch and 680 px (5.4%). TORN means a finite `cut` with `prefix_ok` -- the stale set is a row-major prefix of the successor's write, so the read landed mid-write; the offset differs every run (116, 175, 207, 229, 405, 432, 506) and nothing but a read during a write in flight produces a frontier at an arbitrary offset. COMPLETE means no `cut` and the successor explains every wrong pixel: the successor's write had finished when the read happened, so a skew of one whole iteration rather than a partial one. NO-SUCCESSOR means `successor == 0` with pixels still wrong; on this floor it is pass-2 4x8, the LAST swatch of the test, which has no successor at all. T1 (THE MECHANISM, and it is what this lane's bound is actually responsible for): in arm B, TORN px == 0 and COMPLETE px == 0, on every run. Both are skews and the bound removes the skew, so both must go. FAILS if either survives, and then the bound is not doing what its impossibility argument says -- which is a different and much more useful failure than a non-zero total. T2 (WHAT THE BOUND IS NOT RESPONSIBLE FOR, registered so it cannot be claimed afterwards as an excuse): NO-SUCCESSOR px may be non-zero in arm B. A bound on the guest's run-ahead within the test cannot produce a successor for the test's final swatch, so this class has no successor story and this change has no claim on it. It is 680 px on 1 of 10 runs. If it appears in arm B, S1 of the other prediction FAILS while T1 HOLDS, and the honest report is that the skew is closed and 680 px of this capture were never skew. T3 (THE DIRECTIONAL ARGUMENT THAT SEPARATES THE TWO LANES' MECHANISMS, and it can fail): COMPLETE px must be explained by the SUCCESSOR and not by a predecessor. A texture that was never re-uploaded holds content from an EARLIER upload and therefore cannot show the successor's surface, which is written after the draw that is missing it -- so a missed re-upload does not reach the COMPLETE class, and the texture lane's hash-gate mechanism should leave it untouched. FAILS if any COMPLETE swatch in either arm is better matched by a predecessor than by its successor, and then the directional argument is wrong and the two mechanisms are not separable this way. Noted against it, from #44 itself: on 2 of 11 losses the successor is not UNIQUELY identified -- pass-1 8x2's +1/+2/+3 all match 2,048 of 2,048 -- so this leg is about predecessor-versus-successor and not about which successor. T4 (A CORRECTION TO A PUBLISHED HEADLINE, and it is not about either fix): #44 states that the immediate successor explains 100% of wrong pixels. On the same data, split this way, it is 11,916 of 12,596 -- 94.6% -- with the 680-pixel remainder in the class that has no successor to be explained by. `border_swatch_origin.py` reporting `unexplained_px = 0` is correct on its own terms, because every wrong pixel is matched by SOME candidate surface; that is a weaker statement than the headline, and the two were being read as the same one.
